questions.stem: The box plot summarises the weights of luggage for a group of tourists at an airport.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A quarter of the tourists had to pay an extra charge because their luggage was too heavy.
(b) Write down an estimate of the maximum weight that is allowed before having to pay the extra charge.
(1)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Four tourists with luggage weighing 10 kg, 17 kg, 21 kg and 25 kg join the group.
(c) State what, if any, changes this will make to the box plot.
Give a reason for your answer.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) B1: One extra value in each quarter so no change
B1 for stating "no change" with a suitable reason
eg one in each quartile
one in each section of the box plot
Do not accept within the range or median, quartiles, max, min stay the same or Spread evenly balanced

questions.stem:
The 3 events $A$, $B$ and $C$ have probabilities
$\mathrm{P}(A) = 0.6$   $\mathrm{P}(B) = 0.8$   $\mathrm{P}(C) = 0.25$
The events $A$ and $B$ are independent, the events $A$ and $C$ are mutually exclusive and $\mathrm{P}(A ∪ B ∪ C) = 1$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a)(i) M1: $\{\mathrm{P}(A ∩ B)\} = 0.8 \times 0.6 =$
A1: 0.48
(ii) B1: $\{\mathrm{P}(A ∩ C) = \} 0$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 for use of $\mathrm{P}(A) \times \mathrm{P}(B)$ and at least one correct substitution

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Draw a Venn diagram to show the events $A$, $B$ and $C$ and all the associated probabilities.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) B1: for a box and 3 labelled circles and 0 outside the circles
1st M1: for $\mathrm{P}(A ∩ B) = $ their 0.48 and $\mathrm{P}(A ∩ B') = 0.6 -$ their 0.48
1st A1: for 0.48 and 0.12 correctly placed [If they have an $A ∩ C$ then $\mathrm{P}(A ∩ C)$ must $= 0$]
2nd M1: for use of the addition rule to get $\mathrm{P}(A ∪ B)$ and method for $\mathrm{P}(C ∩ [A ∪ B]')$ eg $1-(0.6+0.8-"0.48")$
2nd A1: for 0.08 correctly placed [plus any relevant zeros if required]
2nd B1: for $\mathrm{P}(B ∩ C) = 0.17$
3rd B1: for 0.15 correctly placed
Examples of Alternatives last 4 marks:
3rd B1 0.15 placed correctly; 2nd M1 $0.8-"0.48"-"0.15"$; 2nd A1 0.17 placed correctly; 2nd B1 0.08 placed correctly
Or: $x+z=0.8$; M1 for $z+c=0.25$; $x+z+c=0.88$; 2nd A1 0.08 placed correctly; 2nd B1 0.17 placed correctly; 3rd B1 0.15 placed correctly
Official notes (completeness pass):
- 2nd M1 $0.8-x+0.25=1-"0.12"$; 2nd A1 0.17 placed correctly; 2nd B1 0.08 placed correctly; 3rd B1 0.15 placed correctly

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: for a correct ratio expression and either a correct numerator or denominator (ft their VD)
$[\mathrm{P}(B \mid C')] = \frac{\mathrm{P}(B ∩ C')}{\mathrm{P}(C')} = \frac{"0.48"+"0.15"}{1-0.25}$
1st A1ft: for a correct ratio of probabilities (ft their probabilities from VD)
2nd A1: for 0.84 or any exact equivalent fraction, $= 0.84$

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) State, giving a reason, whether or not the events $B$ and $C$ are independent.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: for a full reason ft their values from VD Must have 0.2, or $\mathrm{P}(B) \neq \mathrm{P}(B \mid C) = "0.68"$; $\mathrm{P}(B) \times \mathrm{P}(C) \neq \mathrm{P}(B ∩ C)$ is M0
$\mathrm{P}(B) \times \mathrm{P}(C) = 0.2 \neq \mathrm{P}(B ∩ C)[="0.17"]$
[So $B$ and $C$ are not independent]
A1: correct conclusion dependent on having correct values used.
ALT: $\mathrm{P}(B) =[0.80] \neq \mathrm{P}(B \mid C')$ M1
So $B$ and $C'$ (and therefore $B$ and $C$) are not independent A1

questions.stem: The journey time for Charlie to travel to the train station is normally distributed with mean 25 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes. If Charlie's journey time is less than 20 minutes, he will have time to buy a coffee before boarding his train.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the probability that, on a randomly selected day, Charlie has time to buy a coffee.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $[J = $ Journey time$] \mathrm{P}(J<20) = \mathrm{P}\left(Z<\frac{20-25}{6}\right)\{=\mathrm{P}(Z<-0.833...)\}$ M1
$=1-0.79767...$ M1
$=0.202328... = $ awrt 0.202 or 0.203 A1
1st M1 for standardising with 20, 25 and 6. Accept $+$
2nd M1 for attempting $1-p$ where $0.5<p<0.8$. Beware $1-0.83$ (or their $z$ value) is M0
A1 for awrt 0.202 (use of tables awrt 0.203) (Correct ans only 3/3)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
In a particular week, Charlie travels to the station on 2 days.
(b) Find the probability that he has time to buy a coffee on just one of these days.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $(1-"0.202328...") \times "0.202328...", \times 2$ M1, M1
$=0.322783... = $ awrt 0.323 A1
1st M1 for $p(1-p)$ for any probability $p$
2nd M1 for $2 \times$ a probability such that answer is also a probability
A1 for awrt 0.323 or 0.324 [NB use of 0.202 will give 0.322 and lose this A mark]

parts.label: c
parts.text:
On 1% of days, Charlie's journey time is longer than $m$ minutes.
(c) Find the value of $m$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\mathrm{P}(J>m)=0.01 \Rightarrow \mathrm{P}\left(Z>\frac{m-25}{6}\right)=0.01 \Rightarrow \frac{m-25}{6}=2.3263$ M1, B1
$m=38.95808726... = $ awrt 39.0 A1
M1 for standardising with $m$, 25 and 6 and setting equal to a $z$ value $|z|>2$
B1 for $z=\pm 2.3263$ or better (calculator gives 2.326347877...)
A1 for awrt 39.0 (allow 39 from fully correct working)
Ans only For answer only in [38.9575, 38.9585] score 3/3 for awrt 38.98 score M1B0A1

parts.label: d
parts.text:
A new road is built and this should make Charlie's journey time to the station more reliable.
(d) State, giving a reason, what effect you would expect this to have on the standard deviation of Charlie's journey times to the station.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) B1: More reliable suggests reduction of or smaller standard deviation
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for suitable comment that standard deviation should be smaller

parts.label: e
parts.text:
After the new road was built, Charlie's journey time to the station is still modelled by a normal distribution with mean 25 minutes but the standard deviation, $\sigma$, has changed. In the first 20 journeys to the station using this new road, Charlie took longer than 30 minutes on 3 occasions.
(e) Estimate the value of $\sigma$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) $[X=$ new journey time so $X \sim \mathrm{N}(25,\sigma^2)] \mathrm{P}(X>30)=0.15$ M1
$\frac{30-25}{\sigma}=1.0364$ M1, B1
$\sigma=$ awrt 4.8 A1
1st M1 for a suitable probability statement including the 30 and 0.15, may be implied
2nd M1 for standardising with 30, 25 and $\sigma$ and setting equal to a $z$ value $1<|z|<1.5$
B1 for $z=1.0364$ or better (calc. 1.0364338...) If B0 for 2.32 or 2.33 in (c) allow awrt 1.04
A1 for awrt 4.8
Ans only For answer only of awrt 4.82 allow full marks, awrt 4.8 score M1M1B0A1 unless B0 for 2.32 or 2.33 in (c)
